title: Influence of splint therapy on heart rate variability in TMD compared to healthy controls.
summary:
Splint therapy is considered one of the most effective treatment methods for patients with CMD. Among other factors, the method used to fabricate the splints can influence the treatment outcome. Heart rate variability (HRV) provides insights into a person’s state of health and serves as an indicator of the autonomic nervous system, which is subject to sympathetic and parasympathetic regulation of the heart. Since stressful situations are considered triggers of CMD and can also be objectively measured via HRV, it seems reasonable to consider HRV in the context of CMD as well.
The aim of this study is to examine whether wearing a mouthguard causes a change in HRV and to what extent HRV can be used as a potential indicator of treatment success or the severity of CMD. Furthermore, the study investigates to what extent different manufacturing methods for the mouthguards (milled vs. 3D-printed) lead to differences in HRV. 
Both conventional impression techniques and intraoral scans are used to fabricate the splints. 
Over the course of the study, the 60 participants will be divided into three groups, with HRV measured at fixed intervals. Group 1 will first receive a 3-month course of a 3D-printed splint, followed by a 3-month course of a milled splint.
The participants in Group 2 begin the study with three months of physical therapy, followed by three months of treatment with a milled splint and then three months with a 3D-printed splint. Group 3 serves as the healthy control group. The participants are monitored for three months. The results from the three groups are then statistically analyzed and compared with one another.

interventions.name: Participants diagnosed with TMD: After a conventional impression was taken from Group 1 and a splint was fabricated from it, the first measurement for Group 1 is taken one week before the 3D-printed splint is fitted. The second measurement takes place two weeks after the 3D-printed splint is fitted.

Individuals diagnosed with TMD: In Group 2, measurements are taken at identical time intervals. The first measurement takes place one week before the start of physical therapy, the second two weeks after the start, and the third twelve weeks after the start of treatment. Healthy control group: Group 3 will have their HRV measured on three occasions over the course of 3 months. The first measurement will take place during the first week after the start of the study, the second during the fourth week, and the third during the twelfth week.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Age: Age of majority
•	Confirmed diagnosis of TMD (for groups 1 &2
•	Good general condition
•	Signed consent form and consent under data protection law
Exclusion criteria:
•	Age under 18 years 
•	Wearing a total or partial denture 
•	Systemic, neuromuscular, rheumatic, cardiovascular, metabolic, respiratory, acutely inflammatory or infectious diseases 
•	Pregnancy 
•	People with pacemakers, severe bronchial asthma or COPD 
•	Splint therapy that has already taken place in the dental clinic of Erlangen
•	Medications with potential impact on HRV 
•	Acute/past injuries in the face/jaw area with potential influence on splint therapy 
•	Residence with significant geographical distance 
•	People without a smartphone
